es: Reconocer adverbios y adjetivos epistémicos (presumably, conceivably, in all likelihood, undoubtedly, doubtful) y situarlos en una escala de certeza.

teaching.en: The fault was undoubtedly caused by the storm.
teaching.es: El fallo fue, sin duda, causado por la tormenta.
teaching.explanationEs: Undoubtedly (o certainly) expresa casi un 100 % de certeza: el hablante no tiene dudas.
segments: The fault was undoubtedly
caused by the storm.
teaching.audioText: The fault was undoubtedly caused by the storm.

teaching.en: In all likelihood, the power will be back by midnight.
teaching.es: Con toda probabilidad, la luz volverá antes de medianoche.
teaching.explanationEs: In all likelihood = muy probable; va al inicio de la frase, con coma.
segments: In all likelihood, the power
will be back by midnight.
teaching.audioText: In all likelihood, the power will be back by midnight.

teaching.en: The engineers are presumably working on the cable now.
teaching.es: Los técnicos están presumiblemente trabajando en el cable ahora.
teaching.explanationEs: Presumably es una suposición razonable: se basa en lo que se sabe, pero no está confirmada.
segments: The engineers are presumably working
on the cable now.
teaching.audioText: The engineers are presumably working on the cable now.

teaching.en: The blackout was possibly caused by an animal, but we cannot be sure.
teaching.es: El apagón lo causó posiblemente un animal, pero no podemos estar seguros.
teaching.explanationEs: Possibly deja abierta la posibilidad: puede que sí y puede que no.
segments: The blackout was possibly caused by an
animal, but we cannot be sure.
teaching.audioText: The blackout was possibly caused by an animal, but we cannot be sure.

teaching.en: The cable was conceivably cut by a fox, but nobody has seen one.
teaching.es: El cable lo cortó, en teoría, un zorro, pero nadie ha visto ninguno.
teaching.explanationEs: Conceivably = es imaginable, pero poco creíble: certeza baja.
segments: The cable was conceivably cut by a
fox, but nobody has seen one.
teaching.audioText: The cable was conceivably cut by a fox, but nobody has seen one.

teaching.en: It is doubtful that the lights will come on before morning.
teaching.es: Es dudoso que la luz vuelva antes de la mañana.
teaching.explanationEs: It is doubtful that + oración expresa poca probabilidad; el adjetivo va tras it is.
segments: It is doubtful that the lights
will come on before morning.
teaching.audioText: It is doubtful that the lights will come on before morning.

es: Revisar un párrafo de opinión equilibrando reforzadores (clearly, undeniably) y matizadores (arguably, it would seem, tend to) según la evidencia disponible.

teaching.en: Remote work is undeniably popular: the survey shows that most employees prefer it.
teaching.es: El trabajo a distancia es innegablemente popular: la encuesta muestra que la mayoría de los empleados lo prefiere.

teaching.en: Remote work is arguably more productive, but the evidence is still limited.

teaching.explanationEs: Arguably es un matizador: se puede defender la idea, sin afirmarla del todo.
segments: Remote work is arguably more productive,
but the evidence is still limited.

prompt.es: Revisa el borrador (unas 100 palabras): modera 4 exageraciones y refuerza 2 cautelas.

answer.text: Phones are arguably the biggest distraction in many classrooms, but they are not the only problem. Students tend to learn better without them, although the evidence is somewhat limited. The new ban will probably help, but it would seem that it cannot solve every problem. The survey of two hundred teachers clearly shows that 85 percent support the rule. Attendance has undeniably improved: it is ten percent higher than three years ago. Teachers say there are fewer interruptions, but that is only their opinion. To some extent, the ban explains this change, but we should keep measuring the results.

es: Evaluar un rumor del huerto combinando pistas, marcadores epistémicos y evidenciales, y defender la conclusión ante una objeción.
